title: Scopes, rate limits and 429
summary: 401 versus 403, a scope per operation, rate-limit levels, a token bucket, and Retry-After.

steps.title: A scope per operation
body: A **subscription** answers "may this application call this API at all?". A **scope** answers a finer question:
"may this **token** use this **operation**?"
```text
GET  /catalogue/v1/books/{isbn}   requires  catalogue:read
POST /orders/v1/orders            requires  orders:write
A read-only reporting app gets only `catalogue:read`; even if its token leaks, it cannot create orders.
In ASP.NET Core terms a scope is an `[Authorize(Policy = ...)]` on one action. Scopes can also be **bound to
roles**, so only applications owned by certain users can obtain them.
Remember: scope changes take effect when you **deploy a new revision**.

items: A token that expired 5 minutes ago
A valid token from an app not subscribed to the API
A valid, scoped token, but the app's plan of 10 calls/min is used up
A valid token with the right scope, under the limit

steps.prompt: A partner reports: "we get 403 with a valid token on POST /orders, but GET /books works". What is the most likely cause?
options: The token was requested without the `orders:write` scope (or the app may not obtain it)
The partner exceeded the rate limit
steps.explain: 403 with a valid token means "known, but not allowed": a missing scope or subscription. An expired token is a 401; an exceeded limit is a 429; a backend failure is a 5xx.

steps.title: Rate-limit levels
body: Gateways limit traffic at several levels, and they combine:
- **Application** policy: one app across all its APIs.
- **Subscription** plan (business plan, tier): one app on one API, e.g. Bronze 1,000/min, Gold 5,000/min.
- **API / resource** (advanced) policy: everyone together on one API or operation, to **protect the backend**.
- **Custom / deny** policies: rules on IP, header or user; block a client entirely.
When a limit is hit the gateway answers **`429 Too Many Requests`**, ideally with **`Retry-After`** (seconds),
and the call never reaches the backend. Across several gateway nodes counts are shared asynchronously, so
distributed limits are **approximate**: treat them as protection, not precise billing.
> **Practise for real:** **Labs → Live network labs → Live Camel + gateway lab** has a real Kong gateway. You add an
> API key, a 5-per-minute limit and header masking, then watch the 401s and 429s yourself.

steps.prompt: A plan allows 5 calls per minute. A test makes 12 quick calls; the first 429 arrives on call 7, not call 6. Is the gateway broken?
options: No: gateway nodes report counts to the traffic manager asynchronously, so distributed limits overshoot slightly
The plan is really 6 per minute

steps.title: The token bucket
body: The most common algorithm behind rate limits is the **token bucket**:
- a bucket holds up to `capacity` tokens and starts full;
- it **refills** continuously at `rate` tokens per second (never above capacity);
- each request takes one token; with no token left, the request is rejected with `429`.
Capacity sets the allowed **burst**, the rate sets the **sustained** throughput. When rejecting, the time until
one token is available is exactly what `Retry-After` should say:
```text
retryAfterSeconds = ceil((1 − tokens) / rate)

steps.prompt: Capacity 2, refill 1 token every 2 seconds (rate 0.5/s). Calls at 0 ms, 0 ms, 0 ms, 1000 ms, 3000 ms. What does this print?
code: else Console.WriteLine($"{now}: 429 retry after {Math.Ceiling((1 - tokens) / rate)}s");

steps.title: A token bucket
prompt: The tests declare `interface IClock { long NowMs { get; } }` and a `FakeClock` with `Advance(ms)`.
- `TokenBucket(IClock clock, int capacity, double ratePerSecond)`: starts full;

- `(bool Allowed, int RetryAfterSeconds) TryTake()`: refill for the time elapsed since the last call (capped at capacity), then take one token if at least one is available → `(true, 0)`; otherwise `(false, ceil((1 - tokens) / rate))`.
- `double Tokens` (for the tests): the current count **after** refilling to now.
starter: public TokenBucket(IClock clock, int capacity, double ratePerSecond) { }
solution: public TokenBucket(IClock clock, int capacity, double ratePerSecond)
public double Tokens { get { Refill(); return tokens; } }
hints: Store the time of the last refill; refill by `(now - last) / 1000.0 * rate`, capped.
`Math.Ceiling((1 - tokens) / rate)` gives the seconds until one token exists.
template: Dojo.Eq("burst of 3 allowed", new List<bool> { true, true, true }, new List<bool> { dojoB.TryTake().Allowed, dojoB.TryTake().Allowed, dojoB.TryTake().Allowed });
Dojo.Eq("4th is rejected with Retry-After 1", (false, 1), dojoB.TryTake());
Dojo.Eq("half a token after 500 ms", 0.5, dojoB.Tokens);
Dojo.Eq("one token after a second", (true, 0), dojoB.TryTake());
Dojo.Eq("slow refill: retry after 10 s", (false, 10), dojoSlow.TryTake());
public long NowMs { get; private set; }
public void Advance(int ms) => NowMs += ms;
